summary:
Most of this week's sessions went to homelab infrastructure: designing and shipping a coordination proxy that serializes access to a shared GPU across multiple inference backends — text gen, image gen, and embeddings all competing for 16 GB of VRAM without OOM. The proxy acquires an asyncio lock, fires parallel unload calls to idle backends, polls VRAM until the card settles, then forwards the request. End-to-end latency went from random OOM crashes to predictable cold starts under 15 seconds.

A few supporting threads ran alongside: moving the TTS container from GPU to CPU to free headroom for heavier workloads, tracing a ctranslate2 compute-type incompatibility on older Pascal-class hardware down to a float32-only constraint (every quantized path gets rejected at model load), and hardening the inference stack integration so a remote LAN client's back-to-back requests don't trigger a reload storm.

On the phillipsben side, Phases 3 and 4 of the dashboard pipeline landed — wiring Claude's own work summaries and Spotify data into the feed. The pop-os memory snapshot pipeline is live, redaction rules are in place, and the daily cron now writes this tile fresh each morning.
